subject: botany_2
question_text: Differentiate between the following: (a) Dominant and Recessive (b) Homozygous and Heterozygous.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.30, printed question 32. insider_note: Four one-line definitions. Give an example genotype with each — TT, tt, Tt — because a letter pair proves the definition faster than a sentence.

page_header: Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 4 marks

steps.label: Dominant
steps.margin_note: Definition tied to F1, plus a letter example.
lines: The character that IS EXPRESSED in the F₁
generation of a cross between two pure parents.
steps.why: Dominance is defined by what shows in the F1, so the definition has to name that generation.
common_mistakes: Saying the dominant character is the stronger one. It is the one EXPRESSED in F1.
Saying dominant means more common. Frequency has nothing to do with dominance.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever shows in F1 is the dominant one.

steps.label: Recessive
steps.margin_note: Definition, the F2 return, and the both-alleles condition.
lines: The character that is NOT EXPRESSED in the F₁
A recessive character shows only when BOTH
steps.why: The recessive character reappearing in F2 is what proved it had never been lost, only hidden — the single most important observation Mendel made.
common_mistakes: Saying the recessive character disappears. It reappears in F2.
Saying it shows when one allele is recessive. BOTH must be.
steps.memory_tip: Hidden in F1, back in F2: never lost.

steps.label: Homozygous
steps.margin_note: Definition plus BOTH kinds of example. Giving only TT is half an answer.
lines: An individual carrying TWO SIMILAR alleles for
steps.why: Two identical alleles can only make one kind of gamete, which is why a homozygote always breeds true.
common_mistakes: Saying homozygous means dominant. TT AND tt are both homozygous.
Leaving out 'for a character'. The term is always about one gene at a time.
steps.memory_tip: Homo means same: TT or tt.

steps.label: Heterozygous
steps.margin_note: Definition, example, and the consequence. The gamete point ties into the next question.

lines.text: TT and tt are homozygous; Tt is heterozygous

lines: An individual carrying TWO DISSIMILAR alleles
A heterozygote makes two kinds of gamete and
steps.why: Two different alleles make two kinds of gamete, which is why a heterozygote's offspring vary and a homozygote's do not.
common_mistakes: Saying a heterozygote shows both characters. It shows the DOMINANT one only.
Confusing heterozygous with co-dominant. A heterozygote is a genotype, not a pattern of expression.
